lifecycle.headline: BROKEN DOWN FOR PARTS
lifecycle.body: This deck no longer exists physically — its cards were pulled and sleeved into another list. Everything below was true when it shipped and is kept as published; the decklist is no longer maintained.

todo.what: the captain's log — `deck-notes add`; debriefed by the `debrief` agent
todo.how: manamap pilot deck-notes radagast add "<what happened>" --result win|loss --opponents 3

brief.playstyle: Draw-Go Stompy per the PRD v2: a creature-dense mono-green deck that already functions as stompy, which Radagast turns into an ambush deck. Five engines: metronome bodies (3-5 MV, >=2 generic, flashed on every player's turn), flash traps (interaction wearing creature bodies - deathtouch grants, ETB artifact/enchantment removal), per-creature-cast draw payoffs, two-humped ramp (1-MV dorks plus land ramp), and commander insurance. Wins by overrun combat (Craterhoof class), the ambush kill, or a big-mana sink. No combo compression. Interaction breadth floor: >=5 answers spanning artifact, enchantment, creature.
brief.notes: Built 2026-08-12 from the pilot's green bulk (pool-green-bulk.txt, ~298 copies) - the bulk-first constraint is the soul of the project: >=70% of the 99 from the pool, purchases only for measured engine gaps (the audit found per-creature-cast draw at ZERO in the pool). Bracket 3 per the PRD posture (turn-13 close, proactive, no compression); revisit deliberately if the pod demands 4. The commander himself is declared via brief.pool (the one purchase baked into the premise); the bulk file stays a true inventory. Steered 2026-08-12: overrun package pinned (the scorer filled wincon slots with poison chaff while Craterhoof sat in the box); the infect subtheme excluded per the PRD (no poison plan). 2026-08-12 slate approved: six purchases (the gas trio, Guardian Augmenter, two utility lands) declared in pool and pinned — the goldfish measured board density as the binding axis and the gas engine is its fix. Emergence Zone declined by the manabase's own hypergeometric (a 30th Forest beat it); dropped from the slate — one scorer. 2026-08-12 dead-clause purge (the pilot caught Knight of the Stampede): four cards whose text cannot fire in this 99 (Dinosaur discount/copy with one Dinosaur, Mountain-gated menace, plus the daybound coin-flip) excluded; four box cards pinned that fix declared weaknesses instead - Arasta, Hornet Nest, Dawn's Light Archer, Saryth. 2026-08-12 interrogation swaps (doctor-proposed, skeptic-verified): Deathgorge Scavenger in for Essence Warden (graveyard-0 hole, on a body), Hornet Queen in for Briar Patch (the binding width axis; 27 recorded combo lines checked, none live in this 99). 2026-08-12 the $4 trio promoted from the ten after sandbox measurement: Whiptongue Hydra (closes sweepers-0 AND the flier hole), Glademuse (draw per not-your-turn cast - the deck's every-turn action), Yeva (removes the once-per-turn flash cap; commander insurance). Cuts were group-free glue. The measured lesson recorded: this 99 has stopped rewarding consistency purchases; from here upgrades trade small consistency for unmodeled power, and table data replaces simulation as the tuning instrument.

value: Simulates resource development, not full games (no interaction, no removal).
Draw every turn including turn 1 (multiplayer Commander).
Mulligan: keep 7-card hands with 2-5 lands; up to 2 fresh redraws, keep the last.
One land drop per turn when available.

LANDS ENTER UNTAPPED, ALWAYS, and the one in hand longest is the one played. A tapland costs nothing here and no land is ever chosen over another, so this model CANNOT rank two lands that make the same colours — `mana-analysis` and `mana-fit` are what answer a land question, and they are deterministic for exactly this reason.
Mana rocks ('{T}: Add') contribute from the turn after they are cast.
Commander cast on first affordable turn (highest spending priority).
Bodies count = creatures cast + tokens parsed from 'create ... token' text.
Target assembly counts cards DRAWN by a turn (cast cards still count).

CARD DRAW IS ONE A TURN UNLESS `model_draw` IS SET. With the flag on, four channels are modelled — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, and an ARRIVAL trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter (Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent), which rides the same single door the ETB damage payoffs use. Activated draw (needs a spending policy this model has no opinion on), X-based draw (board-dependent), and death- or attack-triggered draw (no deaths, and attacks only under `model_combat`) are NOT modelled and the cards are named in `meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled`. A conditional trigger — 'if you control an artifact', 'you may draw' — is treated as unmodelled rather than assumed to be on: 39 of the 348 ETB-draw cards in the corpus carry one.

AN ARRIVAL-DRAW ENGINE NEVER SEES ITS OWN ARRIVAL. Welcoming Vampire is a 2/3 that draws 'whenever one or more OTHER creatures you control with power 2 or less enter'; registered before its own entry it passed its own gate and drew a card it does not draw, overstating edgar-vampires by 22% at turn eight. The deferral applies to every card and not only the ones worded 'other', which understates Tocasia's Welcome and two relatives by one draw on the turn they land.

ARRIVAL DRAW IS SMALLER WITHOUT `model_combat`, and legitimately so. The channel rides the one door onto the battlefield, which `model_combat` also uses to spawn token copies and ETB-payoff tokens — those are real additional arrivals that do not exist in the resource-only model. Measured on edgar-vampires: 1.264 extra cards by turn ten with both flags against 1.106 with draw alone. Before 2026-08-28 the gap was 1.264 against 0.323, because every call to that door sat inside `if model_combat:` and a draw-only deck silently lost three quarters of its arrival draws.

HELD-UP INTERACTION is reported as two series and both are FLOORS. This model casts everything it can afford every turn, so `interaction_castable` is what a pilot developing at full speed has left over, not what a pilot choosing to hold up two mana would have. A low figure is therefore a real finding and a high one is unambiguous good news.

Tutors are modeled as wildcards: a CAST tutor that fetches to hand or the top — including a TYPED one (Worldly Tutor, Sarkhan's Triumph), which the old literal 'a card' match missed entirely — fills ONE missing any_of group. Consumed once, mana paid, and a tutor that puts the card on top of the library costs a turn. An ACTIVATED, ETB or death-triggered tutor does not count, because this model only knows 'drawn and affordable'; nor does a land fetch, which is ramp and has no channel here yet. Reported as the *_assisted figures; the unassisted figures beside them exclude tutors entirely.

ENTERS-THE-BATTLEFIELD PAYOFFS are modelled: damage equal to the entering creature's power (Terror of the Peaks), X damage where X counts your board (Scourge of Valkas, Dragon Tempest), a token (Lathliss) and a token COPY of what entered (Miirym). Every arrival fires them — cast, token or copy — and a copy is itself an arrival, so they compound, which is the deck working rather than a bug. A payoff worded 'another NONTOKEN' does not re-trigger on its own tokens, which is the brake the rules already had. A chain is capped at 12 deep. X counts the whole board rather than one subtype: exact where the creatures are Dragons, generous otherwise.

The COMMANDER joins the battlefield when cast, attacks, and fires its own triggers. It used to be a mana sink and a flag — cast, then dropped — so a 10/10 flier contributed no power and never swung. Commander tax, death and recasting are still not modelled: it is cast once and it stays.

STATIC cost reduction IS modeled: a commander's eminence from the command zone (live from turn one, unremovable) and typed reducers once they are on the battlefield. It pays GENERIC only and is floored at the coloured pip count, because a discount can never pay a pip. A reduction that SCALES with a board state (Animar, Rakdos, Hamza) is refused rather than counted flat, and cost reduction on artifacts, noncreature spells or a colour is not modeled at all.

Extra card draw is NOT modeled: one card per turn, always. That understates every deck, but by an amount proportional to how much draw it runs — so it is conservative WITHIN a deck and not neutral BETWEEN them. `meta.card_advantage` reports how much of each list this hides. Card advantage is measured nowhere in this suite.

engine.thesis: This is a mono-green deck that spends the three turns which are not yours: Radagast opens one discounted flash window per player turn, a creature walks through each one, a card-per-body engine pays for the creature, and the accumulated board is cashed in by a mass-pump finisher — whose verified kill threshold is FIVE other bodies beside the finisher, not the finisher itself.

diagnosis.verdict: The mana is the best-measured in the fleet's terms (51 Burgess sources vs 36, turn-3 land hit 0.91, commander mean cast t4.0) and the ambush machinery is verified and dense (flash trap drawn 96.1%, metronome body 98.1%). What binds is still board WIDTH: the kill needs five bodies (stack 003) and the goldfish reaches a mean of 3.767 by t6, crossing the bar around t8 (5.313), with finisher-plus-second-wave assembled 40.2% by t6. Coverage is now complete: all five breadth classes answered, and Whiptongue Hydra gives the deck its first sweeper — within Zupke's cap, if far under the control-override band. Stack 005's lesson stands: bodies deploy at end steps (006: they wake attack-ready), the finisher is an own-main cast.

open_questions.question: Whiptongue Hydra flashed in after blockers are declared: does its ETB sweep the fliers before combat damage, how many +1/+1 counters does it keep, and does it kill your own Hornet Nest tokens and Hornet Queen tokens in the process?

Can Scute Swarm alone reach the fifth body BESIDE the finisher? With six or more lands its landfall creates a copy of itself per land entering; how many bodies does the board hold on the turn before Craterhoof, counting one land drop plus a fetch from Wood Elves or Sakura-Tribe Elder?

Does Mirkwood Pathmaker function as this deck's greatest-power dial? With N lands, what is the X on Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex, how many cards does Return of the Wildspeaker draw, and does Selvala's 'power greater than each other creature's power' gate then shut off for every subsequent body — including against opponents' creatures?

Over the board this deck actually assembles, do the other three finishers close? Specifically: on stack 003's exact board (Radagast 2/5, Scute Swarm 1/1, Wood Elves 1/1, Beast Whisperer 2/3, seven lands), what does Overwhelming Stampede deal, what does Pathbreaker Ibex deal on the turn after it attacks, and what does Return of the Wildspeaker's +3/+3 mode deal given three Humans in the 71?

Does the protection stage hold up the two ways it will actually be attacked? (a) Saryth grants hexproof to OTHER UNTAPPED creatures you control — is an attacking Radagast, and Saryth herself, targetable by a removal spell during combat? (b) Guardian Augmenter grants commanders hexproof, not indestructible — does Radagast survive a Day of Judgment, and if he does not, does Heroic Intervention's indestructible cover the rest of a board the wrath is aimed at?
Glademuse reads 'whenever a player casts a spell, if it's not their turn, THAT PLAYER draws a card.' Against a pod with instant-speed decks, does this deck net ahead on it?

How much of the metronome's real output is the simulator missing? The declaration's own note says the sim models neither Radagast's discount, nor aura ramp (Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth, Fertile Ground), nor opponent-turn flash casts.
Can Selvala's tapped mana pay for the flashed cast in the same window (frame candidate line 2)?
How much do the goldfish's three declared blind spots (no discount, no opponent-turn flash casts, no aura ramp) understate board density?

piloting.reading: only 1 game(s) — too few to say whether the AI played this seat like the rest. The rates are reported; the verdict is withheld.

latest.reading: the 95% interval on the win-rate difference is [-0.278, +0.278] and CONTAINS zero. At 10 games per arm this experiment could only have detected a difference of +0.485 or larger, so it is uninformative about anything smaller — that is not evidence of no effect.
